items.question: What sovereign power breaks the ocean of worldly existence through action?
premises: The goddess is sovereign over actions that break existence
She actively performs the breaking of the ocean of existence
items.inference: The goddess both rules and enacts the destruction of worldly bondage.
items.plain_english: She is the sovereign lady of the action that breaks the ocean of existence, and she is the performer of that breaking.

rows.grounds: derived from bhadra with possessive suffix

items.question: In what ways does the goddess embody and bestow auspiciousness?
premises: The goddess is the sovereign of auspiciousness
She possesses and abides in auspiciousness
She gives auspiciousness to others
items.inference: Auspiciousness is her essence, dwelling, and gift.
items.plain_english: She is the auspicious sovereign lady, possessed of auspiciousness, abiding in auspiciousness, and the giver of auspiciousness.

items.question: How are the goddess's form, presence, and dwelling marked by auspiciousness?
premises: Her ears and appearance are auspicious
She is an auspicious mother
She is an auspicious abode
items.inference: Every aspect of her being and dwelling radiates auspiciousness.
items.plain_english: She has auspicious ears, an auspicious appearance, is the auspicious mother, and is the auspicious abode.

items.question: What characterizes the goddess's play, art, and delight in sport?
premises: Her play is auspicious
Her art is auspicious
She desires auspicious sport
items.inference: All her creative and playful activities are expressions of auspiciousness.
items.plain_english: Her play is auspicious, her art is auspicious, and she delights in auspicious sport.

rows.grounds: compound: bhadra+auspicious, vidyā+knowledge; repeated for emphasis

items.question: How does the goddess manifest auspiciousness in knowledge and speech?
premises: She is auspicious knowledge itself
Her speech is auspicious
She speaks auspiciously
items.inference: The goddess embodies and expresses auspicious knowledge through speech.
items.plain_english: She is auspicious knowledge, auspicious knowledge, auspicious speech, and the speaker of auspicious words.

items.question: What relationship does the goddess hold with royal enjoyment, splendor, and form?
premises: She embodies royal enjoyment and splendor
She is the hope of kings
She grants royal form
items.inference: The goddess is the source and support of royal power and majesty.
items.plain_english: She is royal enjoyment, royal splendor, the hope of kings, and the giver of royal form.

items.question: How does the goddess govern royal conduct and inspire fear?
premises: She is royal policy and conduct
She is the fear of kings
She causes fear
items.inference: The goddess controls royal order and wields the power to terrify.
items.plain_english: She is royal policy, royal conduct, the fear of kings, and the one who causes fear.

items.question: What role does the goddess play in generating and increasing worldly joy?
premises: She causes joy in the world
She increases joy in the world
items.inference: The goddess is the source and amplifier of worldly joy.
items.plain_english: She causes joy in the world and increases joy in the world.

items.question: How is the goddess identified with the origin and form of worldly joy?
premises: She produces joy in the world
She embodies the form of worldly joy
items.inference: The goddess is both the mother and the very form of worldly joy.
items.plain_english: She produces joy in the world and is the very form of worldly joy.

items.question: What qualities must a practitioner cultivate toward the guru?
premises: The practitioner becomes endowed with devotion to the guru
The practitioner becomes devoted to serving the guru
items.inference: Devotion and service to the guru are essential qualities for the practitioner.
items.plain_english: Having become endowed with devotion to the guru and devoted to service of the guru,

rows.grounds: demonstrative pronoun referring to the practitioner

items.question: What supreme state does the devoted practitioner attain at all times?
premises: The practitioner maintains devotion day, night, and twilight
Such a practitioner becomes the supreme lord
items.inference: Constant devotion and service lead to identification with the supreme lord.
items.plain_english: by day, by night, and at twilight, he becomes the supreme lord.

items.question: What mastery of scriptures and identity does the practitioner achieve?
premises: The practitioner becomes a knower in all scriptures
The practitioner becomes Shiva himself in all tantras
items.inference: Devotion grants complete scriptural knowledge and identity with Shiva.
items.plain_english: He becomes a knower in all scriptures and is himself Shiva in all tantras.

items.question: What total offering is prescribed for the devoted practitioner?
premises: One should give all wealth as an offering
This includes wife, son, and others
items.inference: Complete surrender of all possessions and relations is enjoined.
items.plain_english: One should give all one's wealth as an offering, and indeed even wife, son, and others.

items.question: What identity is attained by one who delights in this hymn?
premises: One delights in this hymn
Such a person takes the form of Shiva
There is no doubt about this
items.inference: Devotion to this hymn results in becoming one with Shiva.
items.plain_english: O goddess, one who delights in this hymn takes the form of Shiva; there is no doubt.

items.question: What personal benefits accrue to the devotee of this hymn?
premises: He becomes long-lived, happy, and eloquent
His speech is assured
There is no doubt about this
items.inference: Recitation of the hymn brings longevity, happiness, and eloquence.
items.plain_english: He becomes long-lived, happy, and eloquent; his speech is assured, there is no doubt.

items.question: What qualities of wealth, virtue, and wisdom does the devotee gain?
premises: He becomes wealthy, virtuous, prosperous, and wise
He becomes like a guru
items.inference: The devotee attains comprehensive excellence comparable to a guru.
items.plain_english: O beloved, he becomes wealthy, virtuous, prosperous, and wise, like a guru.

items.question: What assurance of mantra accomplishment does the devotee receive?
premises: Success in mantra abides in his hand
There is no doubt about this
items.inference: The devotee gains certain and immediate mastery over mantras.
items.plain_english: O goddess, success in mantra is indeed in his hand; there is no doubt.

items.question: Which afflicted women are identified as beneficiaries of this hymn's power?
premises: A woman whose son has died is afflicted
A woman tormented by misfortune is afflicted
items.inference: Women suffering from loss and misfortune are candidates for relief.
items.plain_english: And a woman whose son has died, or who is tormented by misfortune,

items.question: What further conditions of deprivation and suffering can this hymn remedy?
premises: A woman deprived of wealth and grain suffers
A woman afflicted by disease and sorrow suffers
items.inference: Material deprivation and physical-emotional suffering are addressed by the hymn.
items.plain_english: and who is deprived of wealth and grain, and who is afflicted by disease and sorrow,

items.question: What ritual act brings complete happiness to the afflicted woman?
premises: The hymn should be bound on the left arm
By this act she becomes possessed of all happiness
items.inference: Wearing the hymn as an amulet restores complete well-being.
items.plain_english: should bind it on the left arm, and she will become possessed of all happiness.

rows.grounds: context of speaking; locative sense implied

items.question: In which difficult situations does remembrance of this hymn provide protection?
premises: Difficulties arise in assembly, calamity, speech, and dispute
Danger arises from enemies
items.inference: The hymn offers protection across social, verbal, and hostile crises.
items.plain_english: In assembly, in calamity, in speech, in dispute, and in danger from enemies,

rows.grounds: demonstrative pronoun referring to the hymn

items.question: What effect does remembrance of this hymn have in times of crisis?
premises: Remembrance of this hymn occurs in crisis
Doubt and danger go far away
items.inference: Remembering the hymn dispels doubt and danger.
items.plain_english: O auspicious one, by remembrance of this, doubt goes far away.

items.question: To which unworthy recipients must this hymn not be given?
premises: The hypocrite is an unworthy recipient
The ill-behaved and the miser are unworthy recipients
items.inference: The hymn must be withheld from those lacking sincerity, conduct, and generosity.
items.plain_english: O lord of gods, not to the hypocrite, not to the ill-behaved, not to the miser,

items.question: To which worthy recipients should this hymn be transmitted?
premises: The devotee is a worthy recipient
One endowed with peace and devoted to recitation and worship is worthy
items.inference: The hymn should be given only to devoted, peaceful, and ritually engaged practitioners.
items.plain_english: but to the devotee, to one endowed with peace, and to one delighting in recitation and worship.
